paper_style.palette_strategy: Pastel salmon/lavender/green boxes and black arrows identify the method interface; viridis-like density fields encode intermediate/target intensity; red sample/goal marks and black robot paths are local overlays; orange dashed-square versus blue solid-circle series are stable in Figures 7 and 9; tables remain monochrome with bold/underline emphasis.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1 and table text/rules are vector-like PDF objects; Figure 2 and Figures 3–6 contain embedded raster panels; Figures 7–9 are vector curves/error bars; Figure 10 uses rasterized 2-D histograms with vector axes/text. The review used 200 dpi full-page renders and targeted high-resolution page renders.
paper_style.style_consistency: Proceedings body/caption/table text consistently uses Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern-like math with black rules. Matplotlib-style chart labels are smaller and occasionally sans-like. Main/appendix tables share grouped target headers, direction arrows, ±SD reporting, and bold/underline emphasis; qualitative panels share density/sample grammar while sensitivity panels share orange/blue redundant line grammar.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Objects and updates in reinforced sequential Monte Carlo training. The flows (intermediate targets) and policies (transition kernels) are trained using the TB (8) or SubTB losses (7) on trajectories sampled either by on-policy sampling (forward trajectories from →pθ) or off-policy sampling (backward trajectories from the importance-weighted buffer and ←p).

color.semantic_mapping: Salmon boxes identify flows and policies; lavender boxes identify SMC and policy rollout; green identifies the IW Buffer; black arrows/text define data direction.

encodings.x: Left-to-right/top-to-bottom update flow from learned objects to SMC, rollout, buffer, and return trajectories.
encodings.y: Vertical lanes distinguish flows, policies, SMC, rollout, and the buffer; no numeric axis.
encodings.color: Pastel fill identifies object/operation roles; black arrows and labels identify direction.
encodings.shape: Rounded boxes, arrowheads, and the outer behaviour-policy loop.
encodings.line: Solid arrows and return path encode forward/backward trajectories and updates.
encodings.facet: One conceptual method interface with an outer behaviour-policy loop.
encodings.text: TB/SubTB, pθ, Fₙφ, weighted samples/terminals, and trajectory labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual method interface; no observations, estimators, denominators, or uncertainty. It defines Fₙφ, pθ, SMC weighted terminals, forward rollouts, and backward buffer trajectories.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.1–§3.3 TB/SubTB, SMC, and IW-Buf mechanism → Figure 1 training-cycle interface → Tables 1–4 benchmark/ablation comparisons and Figures 2–6 qualitative consequences.
design_strengths: It makes the mutually reinforcing policy/flow/buffer loop visible in one view.
Arrow direction and stage labels disambiguate forward versus backward data.
TB/SubTB references connect boxes to the formal losses.
design_weaknesses: Right-column placement forces small labels and long return arrows.
No buffer composition, batch size, or update-frequency quantities are shown.
Pastel roles lose contrast in grayscale more readily than the labels do.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a compact method-interface diagram to define objects and data direction first, then reserve performance and uncertainty for separate plots/tables.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Visualisation of intermediate targets for GMM40 (d = 2) across different interpolation schemes. Note that N = 64, F₀ = →p₀ = N (0, σ² I), and F₆₄ = R is the unnormalised target density of GMM40 (defined in §F.1). The “Ground Truth” shows the exact intermediate target at each timestep, which can be derived analytically using π ∝ R and a fixed ←p and is also a GMM.

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis-like intensity encodes intermediate density; row labels are timesteps F16–F56 and column labels are interpolation schemes.

encodings.x: Five directly labelled interpolation columns; no numeric x coordinate.
encodings.y: Five directly labelled intermediate times; no numeric y coordinate.
encodings.color: Density/intensity field in each square, with interpolation scheme encoded by column.
encodings.shape: 25 equal square image panels arranged in a 5×5 matrix.
encodings.line: No connecting line; visual progression is read by row and column position.
encodings.facet: Rows F16/F32/F40/F48/F56 × columns Ground Truth, Linear, Cosine, Learnt, Ours.
encodings.text: Row/column labels and Fₙ/βₙφ symbols provide the key.

figures.data_and_statistics: Each square is a 2-D intermediate density at a selected timestep. The caption fixes N=64, the initial Gaussian, terminal target, and five schemes; no numeric colorbar, denominator, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.1/§4.3 learned-flow hypothesis → Figure 2 shows fixed-schedule path distortion and learned correction → Table 3 supplies target-wise metrics.
design_strengths: Shared row/column geometry makes path deformation obvious.
The ground-truth column supplies an immediate visual reference.
Page-wide placement gives enough area for multimodal structure.
design_weaknesses: No colorbar or density units make intensity only ordinal.
Twenty-five panels and small math labels are dense at page scale.
No field-level discrepancy measure accompanies the qualitative comparison.
figures.reusable_pattern: For an intermediate-state mechanism, use a fixed time-by-method matrix with a ground-truth column and direct labels, then pair it with a quantitative ablation table.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Visualisation of generated samples for GMM40 (d = 2) target in gradient-free setting.

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis-like density/contour field is overlaid with red sample marks; method identity is carried by direct labels and position.

encodings.x: No visible numeric x axis; all panels share a fixed 2-D coordinate frame.
encodings.y: No visible numeric y axis; all panels share a fixed 2-D coordinate frame.
encodings.color: Density field plus sample overlay; method identity by panel label.
encodings.shape: Five equal square panels, Ground Truth plus four methods.
encodings.line: Contour/density background with red x sample marks.
encodings.facet: One horizontal method montage for GMM40 d=2.
encodings.text: Direct method labels under panels; no legend or colorbar.

figures.data_and_statistics: First-seed qualitative GMM40 d=2 sample view. The checked GMM40 helper uses 50 contour levels, clips to bounds, suppresses ticks, and plots at most 500 sample marks per panel; the PDF caption does not state that cap.
figures.evidence_relation: Table 1 gradient-free metrics → Figure 3 direct GMM40 mode-coverage view → Figure 4/ Table 4 extend the qualitative and prioritisation argument.
design_strengths: Ground-truth and four methods share identical geometry.
The montage makes mode collapse/coverage differences fast to inspect.
The source helper keeps axes out of the 2-D visual so the overlay dominates.
design_weaknesses: No colorbar or plotted-sample note makes density and coverage hard to quantify.
Dense raster panels are not suitable for recovering exact coordinates.
A first-seed view cannot establish replicate robustness.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a fixed-coordinate ground-truth montage with method panels and a separate metric table; state plotted sample cap and seed in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. Visualisation of generated samples for ManyWell (d = 32) target in gradient-free setting.

color.semantic_mapping: Contour lines show target marginal densities and circular marks show generated samples; method identity is textual/positional.

encodings.x: Each small panel is one of four fixed marginal coordinate pairs.
encodings.y: Each panel is a shared coordinate projection; only bottom/left panels print labels.
encodings.color: Contour and sample marks distinguish target geometry from generated points.
encodings.shape: Five method groups × four marginal-pair panels (2×2 per group).
encodings.line: 20-level contour lines plus alpha=.5 circular sample marks.
encodings.facet: Five repeated 2×2 projection facets: Ground Truth, DDS, TB+IW-Buf, TB/SubTB+SMC, and full method.
encodings.text: Method labels under groups; xᵢ/yᵢ labels only on bottom/left axes.

figures.data_and_statistics: Four projected coordinate pairs per method for ManyWell d=32. The source uses a 100×100 grid, 20 contour levels, and circular sample marks with alpha=0.5; the PDF is a first-seed qualitative display with no uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 3 establishes the 2-D GMM visual grammar → Figure 4 scales it to a 32-D target → Table 1 and Table 4 provide exact gradient-free/buffer metrics.
design_strengths: Repeated projections make high-dimensional structure inspectable.
Contours stop a sample cloud from being mistaken for target density.
Bottom/left-only labels reduce repetition without removing coordinates.
design_weaknesses: Twenty panels and tiny axes impose a high reading cost.
Projection-pair definitions and sample protocol are not printed in the caption.
Contour/sample hues are difficult to separate in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: For high-dimensional qualitative evidence, repeat a fixed set of marginal pairs by method, overlay target contours and samples, and state the projection map and seed explicitly.

caption.text: Figure 5. Visualisation of generated samples for Robot4 (d = 10) target in gradient-based setting. We adopt the visualisation method in (Chen et al., 2025).

encodings.y: Shared planar coordinate frame; axes/ticks are suppressed in the assembled visual.

encodings.shape: Five method panels with identical robot geometry.
encodings.line: Black solid link segments and red x goal marks.
encodings.facet: Ground Truth, SCLD w/o MCMC, SCLD, TB+IW-Buf, and TB/SubTB+SMC+IW-Buf.
encodings.text: Direct method labels under panels; no legend.

figures.data_and_statistics: The checked visualiser selects 1,000 samples with a fixed random key. Each ten-link configuration is drawn as black solid segments with linewidth=2 and alpha=0.3, black endpoint circles, and red goal x marks; this is an overlaid sample display rather than a mean/uncertainty plot.
figures.evidence_relation: Table 2 gradient-based Robot4 metrics → Figure 5 exposes geometric goal/mode coverage → Figure 6 extends qualitative evidence to ManyWell.
design_strengths: A common coordinate frame and goal marker make coverage visible.
Transparency preserves sparse and dense configuration patterns.
Line and marker shape remain readable without relying on hue.
design_weaknesses: Overdraw can turn many configurations into a black mass.
Caption omits the 1,000-sample selection and goal-coordinate protocol.
The exact five-panel assembly requires run outputs not present in the repository.
figures.reusable_pattern: For structured configurations, draw many low-alpha paths in a fixed frame with an explicit target marker, and pair the montage with quantitative metrics.

encodings.color: Contour and sample marks distinguish target geometry from generated points.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7. Effect of γ of adaptive importance weight tempering. Here and in other figures, the error bars show the standard deviation from 5 runs.

color.semantic_mapping: Orange dashed squares are TB+IW-Buf; blue solid circles are TB/SubTB+SMC+IW-Buf.

encodings.y: Logarithmic EUBO−ELBO (↓), preserving orders of magnitude.
encodings.color: Two method conditions, orange and blue.
encodings.shape: Square versus circle marker plus dashed versus solid line.
encodings.line: Line and vertical standard-deviation error bars.
encodings.text: Legend in right panel; axis titles and method labels are direct.

figures.data_and_statistics: Mean EUBO−ELBO with standard deviation over five runs at each γ. The log y-scale displays low-error and unstable regimes; the PDF does not expose the exact evaluation-window aggregation beyond the appendix protocol.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.4 adaptive ESS tempering → Figure 7 γ sensitivity → Table 5 γ=.05 main setting and Figures 8–9 adjacent sensitivity checks.
design_strengths: Log scale preserves low-error and explosive regimes.
Marker/line redundancy survives moderate color loss.
Five-run error bars make variability visible.
design_weaknesses: Categorical spacing hides nonuniform numeric γ distances.
Shared legend appears only in the right panel.
No exact values or failure counts are printed.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched log-scale sensitivity panels with redundant series encodings and explicit replicate error bars when a hyperparameter can trigger instability.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8. Results obtained from different values of subtrajectory length L.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue dashed squares show the single evaluated method across subtrajectory lengths.

encodings.shape: Square markers; one method so no legend.
encodings.line: Dashed connecting line with vertical error bars.
encodings.text: Panel titles and axis labels; no direct value labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: Five-run mean EUBO with standard-deviation error bars across subtrajectory lengths. Surrounding text defines L=1 and L=N endpoints and notes partial-energy cost; the caption itself omits metric and cost details.
figures.evidence_relation: Algorithm 7/§G.4 defines L → Figure 8 tests quality/sensitivity and motivates L=4 → Table 5 records L=4.
design_strengths: One series avoids unnecessary legend furniture.
Log scale exposes sharp degradation around large L.
Common categorical levels make panels easy to align.
design_weaknesses: Caption omits metric, uncertainty convention, and compute boundary.
Even categorical spacing is not proportional to numeric L.
No exact values or cost axis accompanies the sensitivity.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9. Results obtained from different values of replay ratio I. Extremely large (above 10⁵) values are omitted.

color.semantic_mapping: Orange dashed squares are TB+IW-Buf; blue solid circles are TB/SubTB+SMC+IW-Buf.

encodings.y: Logarithmic EUBO (↓), with off-scale values omitted above 10⁵.
encodings.color: Two method conditions, orange and blue.
encodings.line: Lines and vertical standard-deviation error bars.
encodings.text: Legend in right panel; the caption defines the omitted-value boundary.

figures.data_and_statistics: Five-run mean EUBO and standard deviation across replay-ratio values; values above 10⁵ are omitted. The surrounding text defines I as off-policy epochs per on-policy epoch and chooses I=2 for §4.
figures.evidence_relation: Algorithms 3/4 and §G.4 define I → Figure 9 shows high-ratio degradation/instability → Table 5 and Tables 1–2 bind I to main experiments.
design_strengths: The omission threshold keeps off-scale values from flattening the log plot.
Shared axes and redundant identifiers support method comparison.
Error bars expose unstable runs.
design_weaknesses: Omission is a censoring decision with no count or denominator.
Categorical x-spacing hides numeric distances.
Caption does not state the five-run error-bar convention itself.
figures.reusable_pattern: When a sensitivity curve has off-scale failures, state the censoring threshold and retain an in-band failure audit instead of silently clipping points.

Log histogram preserves sparse high-density regions.
The 100,000-sample count and reference panel are explicit.

First-seed choice does not show replicate variation.
Viridis fields lose contrast in grayscale.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Benchmark results in the gradient-free setting. Here and in other tables, the best and second-best mean values are in bold and underlined, respectively, and we report mean and standard deviation over 5 runs.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over 5 runs; `-` denotes unavailable metrics.
tables.data_and_statistics: ELBO, EUBO, and Sinkhorn for four gradient-free targets; 7 algorithm rows including indented IW-Buf variants, with metric-direction arrows and five-run means/SDs.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.1 gradient-free evaluation → Table 1 principal exact benchmark comparison → Figure 3/4 qualitative coverage and Table 4 buffer ablation.
design_strengths: Grouped target headers make 12 metric cells scanable.
Direction arrows prevent metric-sign confusion.
The five-run dispersion and bold/underline convention are explicit.
design_weaknesses: Dense full-width layout uses small type and repeated metric labels.
`-` mixes unavailable baselines with numeric cells.
Shared columns may invite unsafe cross-target magnitude comparisons.
tables.reusable_pattern: Repeat a two-level target/metric header, put direction in every metric label, and use fixed best/second-best text emphasis in monochrome benchmark tables.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Benchmark results in the gradient-based setting. × indicates training instability (metric is above 10⁵). The results marked with * are directly from Chen et al. (2025).

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over 5 runs; `×` means instability above 10⁵ and `-` means unavailable.
tables.data_and_statistics: MMD and Sinkhorn across five gradient-based targets; 13 algorithm rows ordered by baseline family and proposed TB/SMC variants, with * provenance marks.
tables.evidence_relation: Gradient-based evaluation → Table 2 quantifies SMC/IW-Buf outcomes and failure boundaries → Figures 5/6 qualitative geometry and Figures 7–9 sensitivity.
design_strengths: In-band instability and provenance markers avoid treating missing values as zeros.
Repeated target grouping preserves Table 1 grammar.
Metric arrows remain visible in a dense comparison.
design_weaknesses: Thirteen rows create high visual density around CMCD/SCLD.
Asterisk and cross meanings require caption reading.
External values and failures lack distinct visual treatment beyond text.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep failure/provenance markers in-band, define them once in the caption, and preserve stable grouped headers across settings.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Ablation study of learnable intermediate targets.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over 5 runs; `×` denotes an unstable/failing combination.
tables.data_and_statistics: ManyWell ELBO/EUBO and GMM40 MMD/Sinkhorn across four interpolation/correction variants; nested rows show no interpolation, fixed interpolation + correction, and learned interpolation + correction.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2 intermediate-target path visual → Table 3 target-wise ablation → §4.3 learned schedule/correction stability claim.
design_strengths: Nested row labels mirror Figure 2 decomposition.
Metrics remain grouped by target.
Failures are visible rather than silently omitted.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not define row abbreviations or five-run uncertainty.
Nine columns in one main-paper column force small type.
Readers need surrounding prose to understand the variant hierarchy.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Comparison to various buffer prioritisation schemes.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over 5 runs; one SMC/L-Buf combination is unavailable because terminal-only samples do not define the loss.
tables.data_and_statistics: ELBO/EUBO for GMM40 d=5 and ManyWell d=32 plus Sinkhorn for GMM40 d=50; two baseline blocks compare Buf, R-Buf, L-Buf, and IW-Buf.

The proposed prioritisation is directly comparable within each sampler family.

Metric set is asymmetric across target groups.

tables.evidence_relation: §F.4 and Algorithms 4/7 define knobs → Table 5 makes continuous experiments reproducible → Figures 7–9 vary γ, L, and I around selected values.
design_strengths: Grouped shared values avoid repeating identical cells.
Caption points to algorithm definitions and explains symbols.
The table separates gradient-free and gradient-based settings clearly.
design_weaknesses: Shared blank cells require tracking group boundaries.
No units column is provided.
Target-specific overrides, if any, are not visually distinguished from shared values.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped design tables for shared hyperparameters, but state inheritance rules and units explicitly.

caption.text: Table 6. Ablation study on training losses.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines the learned-flow/policy/SMC/IW-Buf loop; Tables 1–2 establish gradient-free/gradient-based outcomes; Figure 2 and Table 3 connect learned intermediate targets to the mechanism; Table 4 isolates buffer prioritisation. Appendix Figures 3–6 show sample geometry, Table 5 fixes reproduction settings, Table 6 audits loss choices, Figures 7–9 expose sensitivity/failure boundaries, and Table 7/Figure 10 plus Tables 8–9 test molecular and discrete applications.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use italic Figure/Table labels and mostly descriptive titles. Main findings usually appear in surrounding prose rather than short captions; Table 1 supplies the global five-run/best-versus-second-best convention, while Figures 7 and 9 define error bars or censoring locally. Several appendix captions therefore depend on nearby prose for full reproducibility.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Target → and Alg./Algorithm ↓ Metric → recur across result tables. Grouped target headers, metric-direction arrows, mean ± standard deviation, bold best means, and underlined second-best means form a stable table grammar; Table 5 switches to design-parameter rows appropriately.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The Figure 1 objects and arrows map directly to TB/SubTB, SMC, and IW-Buf rows in Tables 1–4. Figure 2/Table 3 test flow learning; Table 4 tests prioritisation; Table 6 tests loss assignment; Figures 7–9 test γ, L, and I chosen in Table 5.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main paper carries the method interface, headline benchmark tables, and one mechanism grid. Appendix G reuses the targets/methods qualitatively and extends to loss/sensitivity; Appendices H/I reuse the result-table grammar for ALDP and discrete sequence design.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Serif/math text and black table rules are stable. Chart text is smaller and sometimes Matplotlib-like, while captions/equations retain the proceedings face. Raster montages trade exact chart typography for sample density, consistent with the checked source routines.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Viridis density is reused for Figures 2–4, 6, and 10; red sample/goal and black path overlays are local. Orange/blue series roles are stable in Figures 7 and 9, while Figure 8 shows the blue series alone. Tables avoid color, so numeric distinctions remain text-encoded.

most_reusable_patterns: A method-interface diagram that names every learned object and arrow direction.
A fixed target-by-method qualitative grid with a ground-truth/reference column.
Grouped target/metric tables with direction arrows, five-run ±SD, and bold/underline best/second-best semantics.
Log-scale sensitivity panels with marker/line redundancy and explicit error bars.
Failure-aware tables and plots that define × or censoring thresholds in-band.
failure_patterns: Appendix qualitative captions omit seed/sample-count/projection details that are only stated in nearby prose.
Compact tables rely on indentation and surrounding text for hierarchy.
Categorical spacing of numeric sweeps hides nonuniform parameter distances.
Figure 9 censors off-scale failures without reporting a count.
First-seed qualitative panels cannot establish replicate robustness.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Define the reinforced SMC/IW-Buf loop once, quantify it with grouped monochrome tables, then reuse fixed-coordinate density/configuration montages and log-scale sensitivity plots to connect mechanism, robustness, and application limits.
